subject.title: compaction: delivery-mirror usage poisons tokensBefore→null; assembler rejects the record, so sessions never truncate (safeguard thrash)

question: Which open fix PR should be treated as the canonical repair for this issue before closing it?
rationale: The remaining work is not whether the issue is valid; it is choosing among overlapping open fixes with different breadth and proof depth.

options.title: Review broader producer and consumer fix
options.body: Treat the broader PR that covers mirror sampling, token normalization, and replay tolerance as the leading candidate if review confirms the implementation is sound.

options.title: Land a narrower mitigation
options.body: Accept a smaller reader-side or NaN-guard fix first if maintainers want the quickest unwedging path and are comfortable tracking producer hardening separately.

options.title: Close duplicate PRs after choosing
options.body: Once a canonical PR is selected, close or supersede the other overlapping candidates to avoid parallel review churn.

recommendation.title: Review broader producer and consumer fix
recommendation.body: Treat the broader PR that covers mirror sampling, token normalization, and replay tolerance as the leading candidate if review confirms the implementation is sound.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main and release-history trail points to Vincent Koc on the central compaction/transcript files, making him the best available routing owner for the canonical-fix choice.
